text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- After the second round of parliamentary elections it is clear that the right wing Homeland Union, with 70 seats, and the Christian Democrats with 16 seats will be able to form the new Lithuanian Government.
- The Centre Union party, which won 13 seats in the parliamentary elections, does not intend to be in opposition.
- The Securities Commission re-registered 201.8 thousand Vilnius Bank shares with nominal price of 500 litas into 2.018 million shares with a value of 50 litas.
- American Walter Diamond will help establish a free economic zone in Kaunas.

- The leaders of Lithuania's banking market are Hermis with a 19.3 million litas profit and Snoras with a 12.3 million litas profit, results for the first nine months of 1996 show. Vilniaus Bank's nine month figures have not been released yet but are expected to show even higher profit figures.
- Lithuania's IMF rep Domenico Fanizza says in an interview that the government will probably not be ready to abolish the currency board when its memorandum with the IMF expires in September 1997.
- The Homeland Union party promises that "there will be no more experiments, distorted reforms or pseudo economy models."

- The leader of the defeated Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party Ceslovas Jursenas compares the party's 12 remaining MPs to the biblical 12 apostles. LDLP intends to form "a constructive opposition," he said.

- American RUMA-USA has proposed to construct a steel processing company in Klaipeda which would cost approximately $10 million. RUMA-USA would like to rent or buy five hectares of land and intends to invest $50 million.
- Bank of Lithuania once again softened the restrictions to Lithuania's Savings Bank in issuing credits. LSB will issue credits which do not exceed five percent of its share capital.
- Mazeikiu Nafta and the French company Elf have signed an agreement to found a joint-venture to produce aviation fuel JetA1.
